name: Utility tiering of ten study techniques
statement: Practice testing and distributed practice rate HIGH utility; elaborative interrogation, self-explanation and interleaved practice MODERATE; summarization, highlighting, keyword mnemonic, imagery-for-text and rereading LOW. The most common student strategies are the low-utility ones.

name: Retrieval practice, the testing effect
statement: Retrieving a fact strengthens it more than restudying it; testing is a memory-modifying event as well as a measurement.
effect: g≈0.51 vs restudy; g≈0.93 vs no activity (Adesope 2017, 272 effect sizes, 188 experiments)

name: Restudy wins at 5 minutes, testing wins at 1 week
statement: After studying prose, restudy slightly beats a free-recall test at 5 minutes (≈.81 vs .75), and testing beats restudy at 1 week (≈.56 vs .42).
effect: recall proportion ≈.56 vs .42 at 1 week; prose, Exp. 2

name: Continued testing holds recall, continued study does not
statement: On a 1-week test of Swahili-English vocabulary, conditions that kept testing recalled ≈80% against ≈33-36% when testing was dropped; continued study of learned items added almost nothing, and students' predicted recall was uncorrelated with actual recall.
effect: ≈80% vs ≈33-36% recall at 1 week; Swahili-English vocabulary

name: Retrieve-then-teach tutor loop
statement: The tutor prompts the student to produce the answer or step before it explains, then grades the attempt; never show the answer before an active-recall attempt.

name: Retrieval always ships with feedback
statement: Testing effects are strongest with feedback, and a failed retrieval without feedback can entrench errors, so no retrieval surface ships without immediate reasoning-level feedback.

name: Ebbinghaus forgetting curve
statement: Retention falls steeply in the first hours and day and then decelerates; distributing repetitions over time beats massing them.

name: Spacing, distributed practice
statement: The same study time spread over intervals beats massing it, and the inter-study interval that maximizes retention grows as the retention interval grows.
effect: 839 assessments, 317 experiments, 184 articles; no single effect size reported, the central result is an interaction

name: Optimal gap as a share of the retention interval
statement: The optimal gap is ≈20-40% of the delay for a 1-week target and ≈5-10% for a 1-year target; too-short gaps cost more than somewhat-too-long ones.
effect: gap ≈20-40% of retention interval (1 week), ≈5-10% (1 year); >1,350 participants, gaps to 3.5 months, tests to 1 year

name: Exam-aware review gaps
statement: With a fixed exam date, set the retention target and review gaps from time-to-exam, following the Cepeda 2008 ridgeline, in place of a generic default.

name: Spacing raises retention about 10-30%
statement: The Data pillar document states that the Cepeda et al. 2006 meta-analysis shows spacing increases retention by about 10-30%.

internal_sources.heading: 1.1 Why spacing + active recall at all

effect: ~10-30% retention increase; population not stated

name: Retrieval improves recall about 50% over restudy
statement: The Data pillar document states that Roediger & Karpicke 2006 show retrieval can improve recall about 50% versus restudy.
effect: ~50% recall improvement vs restudy; population not stated

name: SuperMemo SM-2
statement: Per card SM-2 tracks an ease factor starting at 2.5, an interval and a repetition count; it has no recall-probability target, cannot learn an individual forgetting rate and suffers ease hell.

name: FSRS difficulty, stability, retrievability model
statement: FSRS models each card by difficulty D in [1,10], stability S (days until retrievability falls to 90%) and retrievability R, with 21 parameters in FSRS-6, and schedules the next review where R hits the target retention.

internal_sources.heading: 1.3 The FSRS memory model, made precise

name: Power-law forgetting curve
statement: R(t,S) = (1 + FACTOR·t/S)^(−DECAY); a power law fits because a population of memories with different stabilities decays as a superposition of exponentials. At target retention 0.90 the interval equals S.
effect: FSRS-5: FACTOR 19/81, DECAY 0.5

name: Three stability-gain laws
statement: Stability grows more after a successful recall when difficulty is low, when prior stability is low, and when retrievability at review time is low.

name: FSRS scheduling efficiency against SM-2
statement: On an open benchmark of about 700M Anki reviews FSRS needs about 20-30% fewer reviews than SM-2 for equal retention; the KDD '22 SSP-MMC result on 220M MaiMemo logs reports +12.6% over prior schedulers.
effect: ~20-30% fewer reviews for equal retention (Anki users); +12.6% over prior schedulers (220M MaiMemo review logs)

name: Per-user FSRS parameter fitting
statement: Fit the 21 weights to a user's review history by maximum likelihood with back-propagation through time and recency weighting; ship population defaults and re-optimize at about 1,000 reviews.

internal_sources.heading: 1.4 How parameters are optimized per user

name: Target retention below 100%
statement: A review done when retrieval strength has decayed and storage strength is intact gives the largest storage gain, so the scheduler targets 0.90 retention, with 0.95 in exam sprint.
effect: target retention 0.90 default, 0.95 exam sprint

name: Duolingo half-life regression
statement: HLR estimates a word's memory half-life h by regularized regression, with R = 2^(−Δ/h); it cut recall-prediction error about 45% against Leitner and lifted Duolingo retention about 9.5%.
effect: ~45% lower recall-prediction error vs Leitner; ~9.5% retention lift (Duolingo users)

name: Machine-checked scheduler bounds
statement: A Lean file proves that the clamped difficulty stays within its range, stability stays at or above its floor, and the scheduled interval stays between 1 and 3650.

name: Interleaving problem types
statement: Mixing problem types within a practice set lowers in-session performance and raises delayed test accuracy, chiefly by teaching which procedure a problem calls for.
effect: next-day accuracy ≈63% vs ≈20% (Rohrer & Taylor 2007); ≈77% vs 38% (Taylor & Rohrer 2010)

name: Classroom interleaving RCT in seventh-grade math
statement: 126 seventh-graders practiced for about 3 months; on a surprise test about 1 month later interleaved practice scored ≈80% against ≈38% for blocked.
effect: ≈80% vs ≈38%; 126 seventh-graders; follow-up RCTs d≈0.83

name: Learners feel blocking works better
statement: In every interleaving study learners judge blocked practice as better because it gives higher in-session performance and a false sense of mastery.

name: Interleave confusable sibling atoms
statement: Mix atoms that share requires or unlocks neighborhoods in the dependency graph, since interleaving helps most when items are confusable and need discrimination.

name: Desirable difficulties
statement: Conditions that slow acquisition and depress short-term performance, such as spacing, interleaving, varied practice and testing, enhance long-term retention and transfer; a difficulty is desirable only if the learner can overcome it through successful retrieval.

name: New Theory of Disuse
statement: Memory has storage strength, which only increases, and retrieval strength, which decays; conditions that lower momentary retrieval strength can build more storage strength.

name: Learning differs from performance
statement: The methods that work feel worse in the session than the methods that do not, so learners choose wrong; this argues for system-imposed scheduling and diagnostic progress signals.

name: Dual coding theory
statement: Verbal and visual systems are functionally independent and interconnected; an item encoded in both has two retrieval routes and additive memory.

name: Picture superiority effect
statement: After one exposure to about 600 items recognition was ≈90% for words and ≈98% for pictures (Shepard 1967); recognition was about 83% over 10,000 images (Standing 1973).
effect: ≈98% pictures vs ≈90% words (Shepard 1967); ~83% over 10,000 images (Standing 1973)

name: Mayer's multimedia principles with median effect sizes
statement: Words plus pictures beat words alone (d≈1.35); spatial contiguity d≈1.10, temporal contiguity d≈1.22, coherence d≈0.86, redundancy d≈0.86, modality d≈0.76, segmenting d≈0.70-0.79, pre-training d≈0.46-0.85, signaling d≈0.41.

internal_sources.heading: 1.6 Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning

effect: multimedia median d≈1.35; coherence d≈0.86 (Mayer's own syntheses)

name: Seductive details reduce learning
statement: Interesting but irrelevant material, including images, hurts retention (d = −0.30) and transfer (d = −0.48), and is worst for low-prior-knowledge learners.
effect: retention d = −0.30, transfer d = −0.48 (Rey 2012); 58 studies (Sundararajan & Adesope 2020)

name: Cognitive load theory
statement: Working memory is small; extraneous load from decorative visuals, split attention and redundancy leaves less capacity for germane schema building.

internal_sources.heading: 6: Cognitive Load and the Expertise Reversal Effect

name: Load-bearing art contract
statement: Every generated image must depict the idea, pair image with word, place labels on the relevant part, signal the essential element, be distinctive, and follow pre-training of component names; decorative art is banned.

name: Worked examples and the expertise reversal effect
statement: Novices learn more from studying worked examples than from unsupported problem solving; as expertise grows the same support becomes redundant and can harm.

name: Fade worked examples as mastery rises
statement: Show full worked derivations to novices, then remove steps in a completion sequence and move the learner from studying solutions to generating them as the mastery estimate climbs.

name: Self-explanation
statement: Students who explain why each step of a worked example follows learn more than those who do not, and prompting the explanation induces the effect.

name: Teach-back and the protégé effect
statement: The learner explains the concept to the tutor or a protégé who probes for gaps; generating an explanation for someone else forces elaborative retrieval and surfaces holes.

name: Recall, Apply, Derive, Teach ladder
statement: Mastery of an atom is retrieval at increasing depth: recall or cloze, apply to a new instance, derive from prerequisites, teach back.

internal_sources.heading: 2. Unit of knowledge: the Concept Atom

name: Productive failure
statement: Attempting a novel problem before being taught the method, even when the attempt fails, gives better conceptual understanding and transfer than instruction first, provided consolidation follows.

name: Bloom's 2 sigma claim
statement: One-to-one tutoring with mastery learning moved the average student about 2σ above a conventional class, and group mastery learning alone about 1σ; the source data were two small unpublished dissertations.
effect: ≈2σ tutoring plus mastery (Anania ≈2.0σ, Burke ≈2.3σ); ≈1σ group mastery

name: Tutoring effects in randomized trials
statement: A meta-analysis of 96 randomized tutoring trials found a mean effect of about 0.37σ and none reached 2σ; real high-dosage tutoring gives about 0.3-0.5σ.
effect: mean ≈0.37σ across 96 tutoring RCTs; a large education RCT effect is ≈0.20σ (Kraft 2020)

name: Mastery learning programs
statement: Across 108 evaluations mastery learning averaged about 0.5σ, larger for weaker students, larger on aligned local tests, and partly bought with more time on task.
effect: ≈0.5σ average (LFM ≈0.59σ, PSI ≈0.49σ); 108 evaluations

name: Mastery gating on the prerequisite graph
statement: Do not open the next concept until the current one is mastered, and never present an atom before its requires prerequisites are mastered; the dependency graph is the gate.

name: Interaction plateau in tutoring systems
statement: Human tutoring d≈0.79, intelligent tutoring systems d≈0.76, answer-based computer instruction d≈0.31; the decisive gain comes from answer-level to step-level feedback, and full dialogue adds little.

internal_sources.heading: 2. Intelligent Tutoring Systems, the key result
5: Feedback and the ITS Interaction Plateau

effect: human tutoring d≈0.79; ITS d≈0.76; answer-based CAI d≈0.31

name: Tutoring-system effects at scale
statement: Median ITS effect ≈0.66σ (Kulik & Fletcher 2016), larger on aligned tests; Cognitive Tutor Algebra I gave +0.21σ in year 2 (Pane/RAND 2014).
effect: median ITS ≈0.66σ; Cognitive Tutor Algebra I +0.21σ in year 2

name: K-12 math tutoring systems average near zero
statement: A meta-analysis of intelligent tutoring systems in K-12 mathematics found an overall effect of g≈0.09, not significant, near zero or slightly negative for low achievers and larger with a full school year of use.
effect: g≈0.09 (ns); K-12 mathematics

name: Feedback effects are large and variable
statement: Feedback is among the most powerful influences on learning (synthesis ≈0.79σ) and about 32% of feedback effects are negative; effective feedback answers where am I going, how am I going, where to next, at the process and self-regulation level.
effect: ≈0.79σ; ~32% of feedback effects negative (attributed to Kluger & DeNisi)

name: Step-level, process-level feedback
statement: Grade and respond to the reasoning step, never the bare answer or praise; an LLM can reach step-level feedback without full open-ended dialogue.
effect: ≈0.3 → ≈0.76 jump from answer-level to step-level

name: Guardrailed AI tutor against active lecture
statement: In a crossover RCT with 194 Harvard physics students a prompt-engineered AI tutor more than doubled learning gains against active lecture in less time (median 49 minutes).
effect: ≈0.63σ (ceiling-corrected 0.73-1.3σ); N=194 Harvard physics

name: Unguarded LLM help harms unassisted performance
statement: Among about 1,000 high-schoolers on math practice, unguarded GPT-4 raised assisted scores 48% and dropped the unassisted exam 17% against control; a guardrailed tutor that gave hints and withheld answers erased the harm.
effect: +48% assisted, −17% unassisted vs control; ~1,000 high-schoolers

name: Socratic, answer-withholding tutor
statement: The tutor asks questions and gives hints, never solutions; answer-withholding is a hard requirement, and the outcome to measure is the unassisted one.

name: Khanmigo has no published outcomes trial
statement: Khanmigo uses a Socratic answer-withholding design and grew from about 68k to about 700k users, with no published learning-outcomes RCT.
effect: ~68k → ~700k users

name: Claim only the replicated effect band
statement: Product targets and external claims cite the replicated ITS and guardrailed-LLM band of about 0.5-0.8σ and mastery learning at about 0.5σ, never Bloom's 2σ.

name: Scaffolding and the zone of proximal development
statement: A tutor supports a learner through what they cannot yet do alone and withdraws support as competence grows; scaffolding has six tutoring functions: recruitment, reduction of degrees of freedom, direction maintenance, marking critical features, frustration control, demonstration.

internal_sources.heading: 11: Scaffolding and the Zone of Proximal Development

name: Deliberate practice
statement: Expert performance is built by sustained effortful practice aimed at weaknesses at the edge of ability, with feedback; a later meta-analysis found it explained about 26% of variance in games, 21% in music and 4% in education.
effect: ~26% of variance in games, ~21% music, ~4% education

name: Weakness-targeted practice selection
statement: Spend practice time where the mastery estimate is lowest and the concept has high reach, at the edge of ability, with immediate feedback.

name: Self-determination theory
statement: Autonomy, competence and relatedness drive intrinsic motivation; contexts that support autonomy and competence enhance it, and controlling contexts undermine it.

name: Expected contingent rewards undermine intrinsic motivation
statement: Across 128 experiments expected, tangible, contingent rewards undermined intrinsic motivation; unexpected and task-noncontingent rewards did not, and positive competence feedback enhanced it.
effect: engagement-contingent d = −0.40, completion-contingent d = −0.36, performance-contingent d = −0.28; 128 experiments

name: Gamification effects on learning
statement: Gamification shows cognitive g = 0.49, motivational g = 0.36 and behavioral g = 0.25, with the motivational and behavioral effects unstable under rigorous-study subsets; effects are context-dependent and novelty fades.
effect: cognitive g = 0.49; motivational g = 0.36; behavioral g = 0.25

name: Duolingo efficacy is receptive and engagement-skewed
statement: Peer-reviewed work and Duolingo's reports support receptive gains comparable to several university semesters, while independent reviews find the literature skewed toward engagement and attitudes.

internal_sources.heading: 3. Duolingo, where it helps, where it's shallow

name: Gamify the needs and keep the metric secondary
statement: Progress is informational, rewards attach to mastery events, streaks are soft and freezable, and every fun mechanic must be causally downstream of understanding.

name: Low performers overestimate their rank
statement: Bottom-quartile performers overestimated their rank by about 50 percentile points; part of the raw pattern is a regression artifact and the overconfidence holds up.
effect: ~50 percentile points; bottom quartile

name: Fluency creates illusions of competence
statement: Ease of processing raises judgments of learning even when later recall does not follow; judgments of learning are cue-based, and the illusion is remedied by test experience and by delaying the judgment.

name: Failed retrieval reduces overconfidence
statement: Retrieval gives a diagnostic signal of what is retrievable and a failed attempt lowers overconfidence, while restudy inflates confidence.

name: Predict, then compare
statement: Ask the learner for a confidence prediction before each retrieval and show predicted against actual; frame a miss as diagnostic signal.

name: Replace felt signals with diagnostic ones
statement: Shallow gamification and the illusion of knowing are one failure: both optimize a felt signal decoupled from durable, transferable competence. Replace controlling and fluency-based signals with diagnostic, competence-supporting feedback.

name: Post-training hurts model calibration
statement: The GPT-4 system card reports that the post-training process hurts calibration, so raw model confidence is no safety signal and verification must be external.

internal_sources.heading: 6. The mechanism we are defending against

name: Faithfulness and factuality
statement: Intrinsic hallucination contradicts the source and extrinsic is unverifiable from it; faithfulness is consistency with the provided context and factuality is consistency with ground truth, and a tutor must be measured on both.

name: Retrieval grounding in a human-verified canon
statement: The tutor answers from retrieved canon passages; rerank, keep context tight, threshold on relevance and abstain on weak retrieval, since evidence buried mid-context is under-used and one irrelevant passage degrades accuracy.

name: LLM citation fabrication
statement: Across studies 18-77% of model-generated citations are fabricated; GPT-4o fabricated 19.9% overall, rising to 28-29% for sparse topics against 6% for well-covered ones.
effect: 18-77% fabricated across studies; 19.9% overall, 28-29% sparse topics, 6% well-covered (GPT-4o)

name: Abstention gated on verbalized confidence
statement: Elicit verbalized confidence, condition it on whether canon was retrieved and gate abstention on it; verbalized confidence is better calibrated than token probabilities for RLHF models.

name: Atomic-claim tutor evaluation suite
statement: Score explanations by the share of atomic claims supported by canon, test against a set of known biophysics misconceptions, and track citation-validity rate and context faithfulness; an LLM judge is screening only.

name: Pedagogical harm compounds over a session
statement: Harm rises from 17.7% in single-turn to 77.8% in multi-turn use across misconception reinforcement, over-disclosure and scaffolding collapse.
effect: 17.7% single-turn → 77.8% multi-turn

name: A confident wrong answer is the worst output
statement: In a teaching product a fluent, confident, wrong explanation installs a durable misconception in the same way good teaching installs knowledge.

name: Nucleus of a field
statement: The smallest set of load-bearing ideas that open the most adjacent understanding: the high-betweenness, high-out-degree core of a branch's directed dependency graph, about 30-60 concepts and master equations.

internal_sources.heading: 1. The thesis: learn the nucleus rather than the textbook

name: Foundations-only canon
statement: The canon holds axioms, real math, laws, principles and primary derivations; the learning system does not try to teach every fact in a field.

name: Concept Atom
statement: The single reusable unit of knowledge: a markdown file with id, branch, shell, type, requires, unlocks, equation, mastery_signal, sources, canon_ref and art_prompt, holding a Feynman-level explanation, the formal statement, a worked example and 2-4 quiz prompts.

internal_sources.heading: 2. Unit of knowledge: the Concept Atom

name: Prerequisite, nucleus and frontier shells
statement: Each branch has a prerequisite shell, a nucleus shell and a frontier shell refreshed from current literature; a learner moves shell to shell.

name: Polymathy through cross-branch bridges
statement: A polymath collects nuclei across branches and finds the bridges, modeled as cross-branch edges such as statistical mechanics to information theory to machine learning.

name: Reach Score for ranking the nucleus
statement: leverage(v) = 0.45·PageRank on the requires direction + 0.30·normalized transitive unlocks reach + 0.15·betweenness + 0.10·k-core.

name: Knowledge space theory
statement: The requires edge is a surmise relation; a knowledge state is a set of atoms closed under prerequisites; the outer fringe is the set of atoms learnable next; a learning path adds one fringe item at a time.

name: Reach-weighted greedy route over the fringe
statement: Build the study path by repeatedly picking, from the valid fringe, the atom with the highest leverage times readiness times depth discount, so no atom precedes its prerequisite and high-reach concepts come first.

name: The graph is the map and the path is the route
statement: The daily default is a computed linear route with zero decisions; the dependency graph is a deliberate second view.

name: Bayesian knowledge tracing
statement: A two-state hidden Markov model per skill with four parameters: prior mastery, learn transition, guess and slip; the posterior probability of mastery updates after each attempt.

name: Item response theory
statement: P(correct) is a logistic function of ability minus item difficulty, with optional discrimination and guessing; used to calibrate question difficulty.

name: Deep knowledge tracing
statement: An LSTM model that gains up to about 25% AUC over classic BKT and is not interpretable; allowed only as an optional re-ranker after an A/B win on retention.
effect: up to ~25% AUC over BKT on benchmarks

name: Mastered means retained
statement: An atom is mastered when every required signal level reaches BKT P(mastered) ≥ 0.95 and its FSRS stability exceeds a floor, so mastery means retained and not once-correct.
effect: P(mastered) ≥ 0.95

name: Proficiency times retention mastery score
statement: Per concept, fuse proficiency P = σ(a(θ−b)) at its lower confidence bound with FSRS retrievability R at a fixed horizon such as 90 days: M = P^α · R^β, aggregated as a weighted geometric mean.

name: Validate the mastery rating against exams first
statement: No public mastery rating ships until it has been validated against real exam performance.

name: Fractional implicit repetition
statement: With separately weighted encompassing edges, mastering an advanced concept credits its prerequisites down the graph, which limits review-backlog growth.

name: Placement diagnostic over knowledge states
statement: An ALEKS-style binary search over knowledge states in about 10-25 questions starts experts mid-graph.
effect: ~10-25 questions

name: Blended study-next score
statement: score = due pressure + frontier value + weakness − cognitive-load penalty; a default session is about 60% due reviews, 25% new frontier atoms and 15% weak-spot drill.
effect: session mix ~60/25/15

name: Projected exam-readiness date
statement: Exam-ready means a target share (for example 90%) of nucleus atoms at P(mastered) ≥ 0.95 with FSRS stability above a floor by the exam date; project by rolling the FSRS and BKT state forward at the measured atoms-mastered-per-week velocity.

name: Gap report
statement: After each session list the weakest atoms, the unmastered prerequisites that block high-reach frontier atoms, and atoms decaying toward forgetting, and feed it to the next session.

name: Anchor-constrained atom extraction
statement: An LLM proposes atoms constrained to the syllabus vocabulary, every field must cite a source span, equations parse in sympy, a separate pass checks entailment, and canon-tier atoms need a human expert.
effect: hold a batch when anchor coverage < 0.95 or entailment pass rate < 0.90

name: Practice and credential firewall
statement: Practice allows spaced repetition, retries and self-report; the credential comes only from a sealed held-out checkpoint of freshly generated transfer items, effort-filtered, exposure-controlled and time-decaying. Self-report affects scheduling only.

name: Transfer items generated by construction
statement: Generate transfer items from template skeletons with LLM scenario wrappers, multi-hop from the graph, Bloom-targeted, with distractors from error models; grade with symbolic equivalence where possible and use LLM judges only in ensembles with adversarial canaries.

name: A trustworthy credential's score is inseparable from doing the task
statement: A credential is trustworthy only if the score is mechanically inseparable from doing the real thing, as with chess Elo, the Duolingo English Test and Kaggle's hidden test set.

name: Mastery Profile as a verifiable resume
statement: The learning map becomes a public profile showing mastered concepts, a per-branch rating with visible uncertainty (Glicko-style), per-concept depth, recency and an evidence trail of derivation transcripts and teach-backs, issued as an Open Badges 3.0 / W3C VC 2.0 credential.

name: Skills-based hiring is wanted and rarely used
statement: About 85% of firms want skills-based hiring and about 0.14% of hires use it; in credentialing markets the verifier pays and the learner does not.
effect: ~85% of firms; ~0.14% of hires

name: No product spans more than two of four capabilities
statement: The four capabilities that produce durable, provable learning are a per-learner retention engine, a typed prerequisite graph, thorough AI lessons for any topic, and a verifiable canon-grounded mastery profile; no competitor has more than two.

name: Learn, master, author, share
statement: Learners become the canon's authors: a learner who writes a strong atom or derivation publishes it with attribution.

name: Order-of-magnitude grading tolerance
statement: An estimate a is Correct against b when both are positive and max(a,b)² ≤ 10·min(a,b)², which is a ratio under √10; a Close answer is always Correct.
effect: ratio < √10

name: Unmet prerequisite closure is the minimum plan
statement: For a complete mandatory-prerequisite graph with consistent initial mastery, every valid learning sequence reaching target t contains each unmet member of t's prerequisite closure, and a certified ordering of that set attains the minimum number of steps |R(t,M)|.

internal_sources.heading: Necessity of the prerequisite closure; Sufficiency and minimum distance

name: Minimum fixed effort plan
statement: With fixed nonnegative per-concept costs the certified sequence minimizes total effort, equal to the sum of costs over the unmet closure.

name: A shortest concept chain can omit a required branch
statement: In a diamond where F precedes A and B and both precede T, the chain F, A, T omits B; the valid plan has four steps.

name: Current mastery, historical attainment and unknown
statement: Current mastery is accepted evidence for present readiness; historical attainment records earlier achievement; unknown means unassessed and supplies no positive evidence.

internal_sources.heading: Legend of terminology and notation, Mastery and attainment

name: Reading records activity, assessment records mastery
statement: Reading a page or a client progress flag cannot count as mastery; only an authorized assessment writer records evidence used for mastery.

name: Initial certified-mastery rule
statement: Twelve correct server-scored independent items across at least two forms and two sessions seven days apart, no hints, evidence at most 30 days old; the 95% Wilson lower bound exceeds 0.75 for 12 of 12.
effect: Wilson 95% lower bound > 0.75 for 12/12

name: Catalog coverage G and radial extent r
statement: Each concept splits weight one across its distinct primitive supports; g_j is the confirmed share on axis j, G equals the fraction of catalog concepts confirmed, and G ≤ r ≤ √G.

internal_sources.heading: Constructing the knowledge coordinates; What the coverage measure proves

name: Planner agrees with exhaustive search on synthetic graphs
statement: Across 1,099 DAGs of one to five nodes and 57,060 mastery and target cases the closure planner had zero distance, omission and readiness errors against breadth-first state search.
effect: 0 errors in 57,060 synthetic cases

name: Synthetic response prediction and residual check
statement: On 1,200 synthetic learners Brier scores were 0.24633 intercept-only, 0.23475 item baseline and 0.18649 with axis and prerequisite covariates; a planted residual pair showed correlation 0.33463.
effect: Brier 0.18649 vs 0.23475; synthetic learners

name: Promotion gates for a mastery model
statement: Brier improvement of at least 0.01 over the strongest prespecified baseline with a positive 95% learner-bootstrap interval, expected calibration error at most 0.05, and no subgroup Brier degradation above 0.02.

name: Graph structure does not validate a learning progression
statement: Proposed learning maps need empirical checks; graph structure alone does not validate a learning progression.

name: Classroom studies measure delayed transfer on unseen items
statement: The classroom primary outcome is delayed transfer on unseen items with a fixed curriculum and a teacher-time measure; an underpowered pilot supports feasibility only.

name: Retrieval performance is no education outcome
statement: Retrieval performance cannot substitute for education outcomes, and source-citation prediction is a different target from subject mastery.

name: Teacher preparation as the first education use
statement: A teacher uses evidence search to find sources and passages for a concept or assignment and approves material before it enters a learner-facing lesson.

name: Hybrid retrieval beats pure vector search
statement: Hybrid vector plus keyword retrieval beats pure vector by about 10-15% on accuracy, with keyword search rescuing equations, symbols and proper nouns.
effect: ~10-15% accuracy

name: Hook model
statement: A habit loop of trigger, action, variable reward and investment, repeated until internal triggers replace external ones.

internal_sources.heading: 2a. The Hook Model applied to learning

name: Facilitator test for habit mechanics
statement: A mechanic ships only if it improves the learner's understanding and the maker would be happy receiving it; a mechanic that only lifts metrics is cut.

name: Streak retention figures
statement: Users with 7+ day streaks retain at about 2.4×; a 7-day streak goes with about 90% day-30 retention against about 20%; Streak Freeze cut churn about 21% for at-risk users.
effect: ~2.4× retention; ~90% vs ~20% D30; −21% churn (Duolingo users)

name: Learning-counted streak
statement: A day counts only when due reviews are completed with recall attempts; freezes and rest days are generous; a lapsed streak is earned back by clearing overdue reviews; the streak count is never monetized.

name: Value-led reminders
statement: Notify about real due reviews, at the time this user studies, opt-in, capped at one a day, in an encouraging tone; guilt framing tested 5-8% more effective at Duolingo and is rejected.
effect: guilt tone 5-8% more effective (Duolingo)

name: Co-op social learning by default
statement: Default social modes are friend streaks and cohorts that advance together; competitive leagues are opt-in and scored on mastery-weighted XP.
effect: leagues +25% lesson completion; Friend Streak users 22% more likely to finish the daily lesson (Duolingo)

name: Cohorts and reading groups
statement: A group walks a branch's nucleus path together with a shared daily concept; the document calls a reading group how scholars have always learned foundations.

internal_sources.heading: 4b. Why cohorts/reading-groups are the strategic bet

name: Activation metric
statement: A new learner who completes at least 3 nucleus concepts across at least 2 distinct days in week 1 and establishes a 3-day learning streak.

name: Day 7 as the habit checkpoint

name: Knowledge state, closed state and frontier
statement: The catalog is a DAG of concepts with a mandatory-prerequisite relation; a knowledge state is a set K of concepts, closed when every immediate prerequisite of a member is a member; a concept outside K is ready, on the frontier, when all its prerequisites lie in K.
formal: Closed, Required, Path, After (papers/human-ai-multiplier/lean/Bucket/Learning.lean; same in lean/BucketMath/Learning.lean)

name: Necessary additions
statement: From a closed mastery state, every feasible learning sequence that reaches target t contains every concept in R(t, M) = C(t) minus M, so its length is at least |R(t, M)|.

name: Attained minimum learning path
statement: Listing each element of R(t, M) once in a prerequisite-first order is feasible, reaches t, and attains the minimum length |R(t, M)|; with fixed costs the same order attains the minimum effort.

name: More mastery never lengthens the path
statement: If M1 is a subset of M2 then R(t, M2) is a subset of R(t, M1) and the remaining distance does not grow.

name: Diamond: chain planning undercounts
statement: With F to A, F to B, A to T, B to T and empty mastery, the chain F, A, T never reaches T; any feasible sequence needs four steps.

internal_sources.heading: §The minimum prerequisite learning problem, Figure prereq

name: Assumptions A1 to A5
statement: The theorems hold when every encoded edge is mandatory and none is missing (A1), the closure is finite (A2), restricted mastery is closed (A3), a step adds one concept and nothing is forgotten in the episode (A4), and costs are fixed (A5). "A1 ... is a property of the curriculum that no proof can supply."

internal_sources.heading: §The minimum prerequisite learning problem; §Limitations, The three connecting rules

name: Knowledge region: coverage G and extent r
statement: With confirmed flags m(v) on a catalog factored over axes, g_j is the confirmed share on axis j, G the catalog share confirmed, and r the weighted root mean square of g_j; G <= r <= sqrt(G), and none decreases when flags only rise.
formal: coverage_monotone, squared_extent_monotone (papers/human-ai-multiplier/lean/Bucket/Learning.lean; lean/BucketMath/Learning.lean) cover natural-number cases only

name: Planner matches brute force on small graphs
statement: Across 1,099 DAGs of one to five nodes and 57,060 cases, the candidate planner's distance error, omitted-required count and readiness-error count against an independent breadth-first search were all zero.
effect: 0 errors in 57,060 enumerated cases; synthetic graphs, no people

name: Synthetic learner prediction experiment
statement: On 1,200 synthetic learners, Brier scores were 0.24633 (intercept), 0.23475 (item effects) and 0.18649 (axis and prerequisite covariates) on 4,800 test responses.

internal_sources.heading: §Learning system results, Statistical experiment, Table ls

effect: Brier reduction 0.04826 over the item baseline; 600 synthetic test learners

name: FSRS-5 retrievability as shipped
statement: Predicted recall t days after a review at stability S is R(t, S) = (1 + F t/S)^(-1/2) with F = 0.9^(-2) - 1 = 19/81, so R(S, S) = 0.9; stability and difficulty update with 19 default weights.

name: Mastery as shipped
statement: "mastery is their product": M = P^alpha R^beta with P = sigma(theta - b_apply), b_apply = -0.2, R = R(90, S), alpha = beta = 1, clipped to [0, 1]; "a concept counts as mastered at M >= 0.7".

name: Four artefacts that mimic an effect
statement: Ceilings, task drift between probes, regression to the mean and the practice effect of the retest can each mimic or hide a gain; the design answers with matched pairs, a within-item retest, a planned no-AI control arm and reading L as a between-half difference.

name: Human plus AI against the better single agent
statement: The multiplier paper: "a meta-analysis across 106 experiments finds that human and AI together score below the better of the two on average".

name: Explanations raise acceptance right or wrong
statement: A user study of AI explanations found explanations raised acceptance of the model's answer whether it was right or wrong; team performance above both human and AI alone was rare.

name: Gains inside the model's competence, losses outside
statement: "The jagged frontier study randomized consultants to model access and found gains inside the model's competence and losses outside it".

name: Largest gains for least experienced workers
statement: "the customer-support study found the largest gains for the least experienced workers".

name: Unrestricted AI raised practice scores and lowered exam scores
statement: In a randomized study of high school mathematics, model access raised practice scores and lowered unaided exam scores; exam scores "fell where the model gave answers and held where it gave hints".
effect: practice performance about +48%, unassisted exam performance about -17% (unrestricted GPT-4 arm); high school mathematics students

name: Testing effect
statement: Retrieval practice produces more durable retention than equal restudy, and the advantage grows with the retention interval. The multiplier paper adds that a weekly unaided retest "is itself a retrieval event that raises later recall".

name: People remember where over what
statement: People encode the location of information they expect to look up later at a higher rate than the information itself, across four studies.

name: Ironies of automation
statement: Automating a task removes the operator's routine practice at it, so the human is asked to perform or monitor at the moment they are least prepared; the more reliable the automation, the less chance to keep the skill.

name: LLM essay writing and weaker recall
statement: An EEG study (n=54) of essay writing found LLM users showed the weakest brain connectivity, lowest sense of ownership and most trouble quoting their own essay.
effect: n=54; no effect size recorded

name: AI use correlates with lower critical-thinking scores
statement: A survey and interview study (n about 666) found a strong negative correlation between frequent AI-tool use and critical-thinking scores, mediated by cognitive offloading.
effect: n about 666; correlation size not given

name: AI helps learning only when the learner does the thinking
statement: "offloading the productive struggle can suppress the learning it was meant to support"; "AI helps learning" "depends entirely on whether the design forces the learner to do the thinking or lets them skip it."

name: Bloom's two sigma
statement: One-to-one mastery tutoring moved the average student about two standard deviations above conventionally taught peers.
effect: 2.0 SD; students under one-to-one mastery tutoring against conventional classes

name: Mastery learning programs: about half a standard deviation
statement: "Across 108 controlled studies, group-based mastery learning raised scores by about 0.5 SD, well below Bloom 1984's two-sigma figure".
effect: about 0.5 SD; 108 controlled studies of group-based mastery learning

name: Step-based tutoring nears human tutoring
statement: "Step-based intelligent tutoring systems (feedback on intermediate steps) approach human-tutoring effect size (~0.75-1 SD); answer-based systems reach only ~0.3 SD."
effect: about 0.75 to 1 SD step-based, about 0.3 SD answer-based; tutoring-system studies

name: Intelligent tutoring systems: about two thirds of a standard deviation
statement: Across 50 controlled evaluations, intelligent tutoring systems raised scores by about 0.66 SD (median), with Cognitive Tutor around 0.4 SD; weaker designs inflate the pooled estimate.
effect: about 0.66 SD; 50 controlled evaluations

name: Tutoring at scale: a quarter to a third of a standard deviation
statement: A 2024 meta-analysis found a pooled tutoring effect of about 0.37 SD, falling to about 0.25 SD in programs serving 500 to 7,000 students; high-dosage tutoring is about 15 to 20 times more effective than low-dosage.
effect: 0.37 SD pooled, 0.25 SD at scale; 96+ RCTs per the KAG table

name: Teaching at the Right Level
statement: Grouping children by learning level across six randomized evaluations in seven Indian states produced 0.14 SD in year 1 and 0.28 SD in year 2 (Balsakhi) and about 0.71 SD reading and 0.69 SD arithmetic in Learning Camps.
effect: 0.28 to 0.71 SD; primary-age children in India; about 1.85 years of learning gain from a 30-hour program

name: Metacognition and self-regulation: about seven months
statement: Metacognition and self-regulation rank high-impact and low-cost in the EEF Teaching and Learning Toolkit at about +7 months; "the strongest evidence and the emptiest market cell coincide."
effect: about +7 months of progress; school pupils (EEF Toolkit)

name: AI tutor RCT in Nigeria
statement: A World Bank RCT in Edo State, six weeks of teacher-facilitated after-school sessions with Copilot/GPT-4, found 0.31 SD on the combined assessment and 0.23 SD on English, with female students gaining more.
effect: 0.31 SD combined, 0.23 SD English; secondary students in nine public schools, Benin City

name: Structured AI tutor against active learning
statement: In a randomized within-class crossover, students using a pedagogically structured AI tutor learned more in less time and reported higher engagement than in an active-learning class session on the same content.

name: AI suggestions for human tutors
statement: In a large field deployment, students of tutors with real-time AI suggestions showed higher topic mastery, with the largest gains for tutors with less certification or experience.

name: Platform evidence borrowed for AI tutor features
statement: "strong platform evidence is being borrowed to vouch for AI-tutor features whose own evidence is not yet in": Khan Academy's India RCT found 0.44 to 0.47 SD at high usage for the platform, while Khanmigo efficacy studies are under way.
effect: 0.44 to 0.47 SD at high usage; about 5,500 students in 74 schools in India

name: Ten study techniques graded
statement: Practice testing and distributed practice are high utility; interleaving, elaborative interrogation and self-explanation moderate; rereading, highlighting, summarization, keyword mnemonics and imagery low. 84% of students study by rereading.
effect: 84% of students reread

name: Learners misjudge spacing
statement: "90% of students learned better after spaced practice than massed practice, yet 72%" believed massing was better.
effect: 90% learned better spaced; 72% believed massed was better; students in one study

name: Metacognition
statement: "metacognition is the "active monitoring and consequent regulation and orchestration" of cognitive processes in service of a goal", split into metacognitive knowledge (declarative, procedural, conditional) and monitoring or regulation.

name: Zimmerman: self-regulated learning cycle
statement: A cycle of forethought (goal-setting, planning, motivation), performance (strategy use, self-monitoring) and self-reflection (self-evaluation, attribution) feeding the next cycle.

name: Critical thinking is bound to domain knowledge
statement: Generic, content-free critical-thinking instruction transfers weakly; Willingham holds it is domain-specific. A synthesis of 341 effect sizes found about g = 0.30, largest when taught explicitly and inside subject content.
effect: g about 0.30; 341 effect sizes from controlled studies

name: Structured philosophical inquiry helps
statement: Philosophy for Children: a systematic review found about d = 0.43; a three-level meta-analysis of 53 effect sizes from 33 studies (4,568 participants) found about g = 0.59.
effect: d about 0.43; g about 0.59 across 4,568 participants

name: Schools teach almost no epistemology
statement: "Most school systems contain almost no formal instruction in philosophy, logic, epistemology, or the structure of" argument; the reform implication is to make reasoning, logic, epistemology and argument pervasive inside rich knowledge.

name: Self-determination theory
statement: Intrinsic motivation rests on three needs, autonomy, competence and relatedness; grades, deadlines, surveillance and tangible rewards undermine it when felt as external control.

name: Intrinsic motivation falls through school
statement: Intrinsic motivation fell from 3rd through 8th grade; Gallup reports about 74% of fifth-graders engaged, falling to roughly one third by 10th to 12th grade.
effect: 74% engaged in grade 5 to about one third by grades 10 to 12; US students (Gallup)

name: Curiosity as an information gap
statement: Curiosity is the felt gap between current and desired knowledge; it peaks at intermediate uncertainty and rises when the gap is named and specific. A high-curiosity state raises memory for the answer and for unrelated nearby material.

name: Small payments can do worse than none
statement: A daycare late-fine field study and a matched lab task both show a non-monotonic relation between payment size and the behaviour it is meant to encourage.

name: Cognitive load and worked examples
statement: A novice's working memory is limited; unguided problem-solving search uses it on the search and leaves less for building the schema. Worked examples remove the search demand.

name: Guided inquiry beats unguided
statement: Across 72 studies guidance in inquiry learning helped learning activities (d = 0.66), performance success (d = 0.71) and outcomes (d = 0.50). Across 37 studies inquiry-based science teaching had a mean effect of 0.50, and teacher-led beat student-led by about 0.40 SD.
effect: d = 0.50 on learning outcomes across 72 studies; mean 0.50 across 37 studies

name: Minimal guidance debate
statement: Kirschner, Sweller and Clark argue minimally guided instruction underperforms guided instruction for learners without high prior knowledge; Hmelo-Silver, Duncan and Chinn reply that problem-based and inquiry learning are heavily scaffolded.

name: Project-based learning raises achievement
statement: Pooled across studies, project-based learning raised achievement, with the effect varying by implementation; deep/03 gives 46 effect sizes and about 12,585 students with a medium-to-large effect.
effect: medium-to-large; 46 effect sizes, about 12,585 students (no number given)

name: Research apprenticeships
statement: Across 53 studies, research apprenticeships produced career-aspiration, content-understanding and confidence gains more reliably than nature-of-science understanding gains; duration and explicit outcome focus shaped which outcomes appeared.
effect: 53 studies reviewed; no pooled effect

name: Course-based research reaches every enrolled student
statement: A course-embedded research experience reaches every enrolled student, where an internship reaches only those who apply, are selected and can afford it.

name: Required participation and misconduct
statement: Among students uninterested in a science career who were required to do science fair, about 10 percent reported research misconduct; a requirement reduced the share reporting increased interest.
effect: about 10% reported misconduct; required, uninterested high school participants

name: Lateral reading
statement: Professional fact checkers judge a website by leaving it to check other sources; historians and students stayed on the site and were misled. Across 3,446 US high school students, 96 percent missed a site's fossil-fuel ties and two thirds could not tell news from ads.
effect: 96% of 3,446 US high school students missed the industry tie

name: Information foraging
statement: People adapt search to maximize valuable information gained per unit cost; information scent predicts the path a searcher follows.

name: Learning styles do not work
statement: Pashler, McDaniel, Rohrer and Bjork's 2008 review found "virtually no evidence" for the crossover interaction the meshing hypothesis needs.
effect: about 0 (null)

name: Acceleration helps the top
statement: SMPY: ability predicts outcomes with no right-tail plateau; acceleration about g = 0.70 against same-age peers and helps the top without harming others.
effect: g about 0.70 against same-age non-accelerated peers; about 0.09 against older peers joined

name: Four levels of epistemological understanding
statement: Realist (knowledge copies reality), absolutist (certain facts held by authority), multiplist (unevaluable opinion) and evaluativist (a judged, evidence-based claim among alternatives); the level reached differs by domain.

name: Three forms of meta-knowing
statement: Critical thinking develops through three forms of second-order cognition: metacognitive (about one's own cognition), metastrategic (about strategies) and epistemological (about the nature and sources of knowledge).

name: Epistemological belief research is fragmented
statement: Independent research programs on beliefs about knowledge and knowing use differing definitions, frameworks and methods; the review names nine issues to resolve.

name: Beliefs about knowledge predict comprehension
statement: Students who believed knowledge is simple and certain drew more oversimplified, absolute conclusions from an ambiguous passage than students who believed it complex and tentative.

name: Five components of epistemic cognition
statement: Epistemic aims and value; the structure of knowledge; sources and justification of knowledge; epistemic virtues and vices; reliable and unreliable processes for reaching epistemic aims.

name: Four epistemic positions
statement: Realism, dogmatism, skepticism and rationalism, characterized by how beliefs pattern across three dimensions.

name: Epistemic thinking has cognitive and metacognitive parts
statement: Epistemic thinking combines cognitive and metacognitive aspects; epistemic metacognition has separable skills, knowledge and experiences.

name: Practical epistemologies
statement: A gap separates students' stated beliefs about science from the practical epistemologies that guide their own inquiry; inquiry instruction that ignores the gap stands little chance of teaching how professional science works.

name: Views of Nature of Science questionnaire
statement: An open-ended instrument used with individual interviews to assess views of the nature of science; the authors argue forced-choice instruments cannot capture them.

name: Epistemic beliefs, emotions and complex learning
statement: A model links beliefs about the certainty and simplicity of scientific knowledge to epistemic emotions and then to complex-learning outcomes, tested on climate change.

name: Three impact lines
statement: The research home sorts every item into Education reform ("Open the path from consuming knowledge to producing it, for every learner."), Scientific discovery with ML, and More capable humans ("Shorten the route to mastery with learning systems that build on what a person already knows.").

name: Impact registry figure titles describe results that do not exist
statement: The impact registry titles the multiplier paper's figures "Learning timeline with and without the system" and "Mastery scores by condition".

name: Mission claim: the Academy teaches metacognition
statement: The mission page says the Academy offers "Spaced-repetition mastery over the canon's seven branches" and a branch that "TEACHES the highest-leverage missing skill the research names (metacognition, retrieval, spacing) as content you master"; "Most systems only USE this science; Bucket also teaches it."

name: Founder thesis: AI is holding human capability back
statement: "we are treating AI like it is um turning us stupid. Really, it is holding us back." The measure of a good system is that human capability keeps rising; Research OS exists to "understand the mech-mechanisms and systems and environments in which AI does not degrade us".

name: Founder thesis: education lowers existential risk
statement: "education is extremely tied to the long-term uh viability of the human race"; "education and human capability, human intellect, is all extremely important to uh minimizing that existential risk. And that's why I'm a teacher".
